data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ghara' which means 'to be free', Ghuraisah is the name of a woman mentioned in the Quran who was released from the bondage of ignorance and sin. This name symbolizes spiritual liberation and the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom. The name Ghuraisah carries the meaning “The freed one” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghuraisah usually hope their child will grow to embody the freed one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghuraisah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ghuraisah holds cultural significance as it is the name of a Companion or Sahabi of the Prophet Muhammad peace be upon him. Her release from bondage serves as a reminder of the importance of education and personal growth in Islamic culture. In many Muslim communities, the story of Ghuraisah is referenced to inspire individuals to seek knowledge and personal improvement, especially for women.
data.spiritual_significance: Ghuraisah's name holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the idea of spiritual liberation and release from the chains of ignorance and sin. The name invites us to reflect on our own spiritual journeys and encourages us to seek knowledge and wisdom in order to grow closer to Allah and live a more righteous and enlightened life. Additionally, her name reminds us of the power of repentance and the importance of asking Allah for forgiveness and releasing ourselves from the bondage of our past mistakes. Overall, Ghuraisah's name is a reminder of the transformative power of knowledge, spiritual growth, and repentance in Islamic spirituality.
